nodes.label: FetchContent Integration of GoogleTest
nodes.rationale: Building GoogleTest as part of the consuming project (via add_subdirectory / FetchContent) guarantees the same compiler and linker settings between GoogleTest and the rest of the project, avoiding incompatible-library (debug/release) issues, which matters especially on Windows. FetchContent is preferred over manual download, in-tree copies, or git submodules because it 'doesn't have the limitations of the other methods', at the cost of requiring CMake 3.14+ for FetchContent_MakeAvailable().

nodes.label: gtest_force_shared_crt Option
nodes.rationale: Visual Studio projects link the C runtime dynamically by default while GoogleTest links it statically, producing LNK2038 'RuntimeLibrary' mismatch errors. Enabling gtest_force_shared_crt makes gtest link the runtime dynamically so it matches the including project.

nodes.label: GTEST_HAS_PTHREAD / GTEST_IS_THREADSAFE
nodes.rationale: GoogleTest is thread-safe only where pthread is available; the macro lets users force detection when autodetection fails, and the CMake script handles the required compiler/linker pthread flags automatically.

nodes.label: GTEST_CREATE_SHARED_LIBRARY / GTEST_LINKED_AS_SHARED_LIBRARY
nodes.rationale: Symbol-visibility flags are not strictly required today on compilers like GCC, but are recommended anyway so that a future GoogleTest release that improves library load speed via visibility control does not break existing build scripts.

nodes.label: GTEST_DONT_DEFINE_FOO Macro Renaming
nodes.rationale: C++ macros do not obey namespaces, so two libraries defining the same macro name clash when both headers are included. GoogleTest offers an opt-in rename (FOO -> GTEST_FOO) so the consuming project can resolve the collision without patching either library.
